I do not start from zero. I look at what worked on my land last year, then I adjust a little. I have 14 mu, not tiny but not really big either, so I cannot gamble. Some people in my family work off-farm, so I will keep the field work a bit simpler and put money where yield is most stable. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage. For wheat and maize, I will stay fairly steady because these two crops feed the year’s cash flow. I will use hybrid maize seed, improved wheat seed, enough fertilizer to keep the stand strong, and I will not cut irrigation too hard. Cotton costs more in management and pesticide, but if I keep the area smaller, I can still manage it well. Stevia needs careful fertilizer and water, but the return can be good, so I will keep a meaningful area for it and not be stingy on potash. Around here, if I underfeed a crop and lose yield, that hurts more than spending a bit extra on one more bag of fertilizer. I also watch what nearby farmers do, and I will stay close to that range instead of trying anything too new.
